description: Aurora (XPU) multinode finetune of ProteoScribe (1 block) on cleaned (sequence, fields) records via the generalized dataloader. Composes the Aurora machine base (device=xpu, devices_per_node=12). Intended as a 64-node scaling/infra test of the generalized finetuning path; see notes on global-batch math.
notes: Global batch = batch_size * num_nodes * devices_per_node. At 64 nodes x 12 tiles x batch_size=8 that is 6144; on ~27.8k train records that is only ~4-5 optimizer steps/epoch. Fine for an infra/scaling test, NOT for convergence. For real SH3 finetuning use far fewer nodes (1-8) or many epochs.

Validation runs once per epoch on the full val split (limit_val_batches=1.0 = 100% of the loader). At 768 ranks the val set shards to ~2 batches/rank, so val metrics are coarse but valid (a fractional limit like 0.1 would round to 0 batches and error). training_strategy=primary_only keeps validation epoch-based; val_check_interval is ignored in this mode (it would otherwise be invalid at ~3-4 train batches/epoch). Aurora XPU has shown a first-validation hang on larger datasets; if the run stalls entering validation, reduce node count or limit_val_batches.
weights/ and data/ paths are repo-relative symlinks; they must resolve on Aurora (re-link from /flare/NLDesignProtein/sharepoint/BioM3-data-share).
